support.scope_note: hardware_verified covers the session, capture, waveform download and :MEASure paths only. hardware_evidence.note: the per-claim table is in SUPPORT.md; no single date covers every claim

known_limitations: Arming is unreliable on 4.8.12.1.1.6.5: TRMD SINGLE on an already-stopped scope fails the READY->STOP wait, and arming from a running scope fails the same way on a fast signal because the acquisition completes before the first poll. Legacy capture of the existing stopped frame works.

The modern transfer window can exceed the record: with WFSU NP=1000000 and ACQ:POINts=100000 the modern preamble reports 1,000,000 points while the scope returns 100,000, so every segment is refused. Only the legacy path captures that frame.

Voltage reconstructed from codes can be wrong while the structure status still reads VALID: a reply from another channel is accepted as this channel's V/div (scope_protocol.py query_ascii does not verify the echo prefix), an ampere scale is reported as volts (_UNIT_SCALES maps A to 1.0 and units are hardcoded), a legacy capture never reads the panel offset, and code_per_div is only checked for >0. Five paths reproduced offline in artifacts/check-waveform/report.md.
No cross-check against the instrument's own :MEASure PKPK/TOP/BASE existed at the time of this record, so 'the scale is usable' was conflated with 'the level is confirmed'.

Silent-accept classes remain possible: an unparseable WAV:STAR? readback, a legacy DAT2 capture recorded without descriptor validation, a validator with no point-count authority, and a decode reader whose 'bytes stopped' is not content completeness. See SUPPORT.md for which are fixed.
Probe ratio is never read back (:CHANnel<n>:PROBe? is called nowhere), so vdiv_with_probe is unverified.
Offset sign and the offset*probe direction have no non-zero hardware reply, so they stay UNVERIFIED.
No voltage calibration was performed; derived levels are OBSERVED_UNVERIFIED at best.
The :PRINt? PNG reader and waveform-bundle/v1 export are documented and offline-tested only; offline analysis and evidence reporting live in oscilloscope-waveform-analysis.
Status words are reused across claims: VALID proves descriptor-versus-panel self-consistency, never an absolute voltage.
